expr: (list (progn (string-match "\\(a\\)\\(b\\)" "ab") (replace-match "\\2\\1" t nil "ab")) (progn (string-match "b+" "abbbc") (replace-match "[\\&]" t nil "abbbc")) (progn (string-match "b" "ab") (replace-match "\\\\" t nil "ab")))
note: LITERAL nil's THREE ESCAPES. Emacs answers ("ba" "a[bbb]c" "a\\"): `\\N' is the Nth group's text, `\\&' is the whole match, and `\\\\' is one backslash. The same three `replace-regexp-in-string' already implements in kg (phase15-replace-regexp-in-string, an agreement), which is where 26.2 should take the expansion from rather than writing a second one. kg answers `void-function'. The third element also brushes fe's writer divergence -- a printed kg string does not re-escape its backslashes -- so if this case ever agrees on the first two and differs on the third, that is what it is.
